mathematical_result.statement: For iid Uniform[0,1] in dimension four and A_tau=I_4-(1-tau)J_4/4 with spectrum {1,1,1,tau}, writing Q3=X^T(I-J/4)X and Q_rest=tau((sum X_i)/2)^2, one has sup_b ||p_{Q3|Q_rest=b}||_infinity=infinity for every tau!=0. Thus the scalar-Q_rest worst-fiber bridge proposed in owner revision 2026-09-22.11 is false inside the exact target class.

partner_result_applied.scope_used: A physical 3x3 block with two same-sign eigenvalues of magnitude at least L and arbitrary third eigenvalue gives full-ambient density cap C_*/L, C_*=24.183038289961516... .
partner_result_applied.application: The principal block of A_tau on coordinates 1,2,3 has eigenvalues {1,1,(1+3tau)/4}, so the full law has density cap <=24.183038289961516 for every real tau. Hence the conditional-cap divergence is only a proof-interface failure, not a QFORM counterexample.

unresolved_implication: Find an averaged source-valid scalar-conditioning or fractional-trace functional that retains the Q_rest level weight before any supremum; the worst-fiber L-infinity interface is impossible even with one added eigenvalue.
next_step: Quantify the compensation on the exact simplex family by pairing the O(r^-2) conditional core-density scale with the vanishing scalar-level density, then seek a norm/Hardy-type inequality stable under arbitrary added spectral directions.
